extracted.intended_audience: governments, national trademark/industrial property offices, WIPO, trademark examiners and IP lawyers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for establishing, using, amending and governing the International Classification of the Figurative Elements of Marks under the Vienna Agreement (treaty text and related institutional/financial rules). Targets how contracting parties and competent offices should treat and apply the Classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Classification of Figurative Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification of Figurative Elements comprises a list of categories, divisions and sections in which the figurative elements of marks are classified, together with, as the case may be, explanatory notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Classification must contain categories/divisions/sections and may include explanatory notes; this is the structural content contracting parties adopt (Article 2(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic copies and languages of the Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification of Figurative Elements is contained in one authentic copy, in the English and French languages, both texts being equally authentic, signed by the Director General and deposited with him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments/additions are also to be contained in an authentic copy in English and French signed by the Director General (Article 2(2), Article 3(1), Article 2(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of official texts in other languages
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall establish, in consultation with interested Governments, official texts of the Classification in languages which the Assembly may designate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly decides which other languages to establish official texts for (Article 3(2), Article 17(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and non-binding nature of the Classification on protection extent
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the requirements prescribed by this Agreement, the scope of the Classification shall be that attributed to it by each country of the Special Union; the Classification shall not bind countries in respect of the extent of protection afforded to the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries retain discretion over substantive protection despite using the Classification (Article 4(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted modes of use by competent offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent Offices of countries of the Special Union shall have the right to use the Classification either as a principal or as a subsidiary system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices may choose to make the Classification the main system or a secondary/reference system (Article 4(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of classification numbers in official documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent Offices shall include in official documents and publications relating to registrations and renewals of marks the numbers of the categories, divisions and sections in which the figurative elements of those marks are to be placed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numbers must be preceded by the words 'Classification of Figurative Elements' or an abbreviation determined by the Committee of Experts (Article 4(3)–(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional declarations on omission of section numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Any country may, at signature or deposit of ratification/accession, declare that it does not undertake to include the numbers of all or some of the sections in official documents and publications relating to registrations and renewals of marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows contracting parties to opt out of publishing some classification section numbers in official materials (Article 4(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation when registration is entrusted to intergovernmental authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If a country entrusts registration of marks to an intergovernmental authority, it shall take all possible measures to ensure that that authority uses the Classification in accordance with this Article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must ensure delegated authorities adhere to the Agreement's use provisions (Article 4(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and representation in the Committee of Experts
rubrics_metrics.description: A Committee of Experts shall be set up in which each country of the Special Union shall be represented; each country member of the Committee shall have one vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee handles Classification amendments and advises on uniform application; membership includes contracting parties and may include observers (Article 5(1), Article 5(6)(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Observers and invited participants at Committee meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General may (and shall if requested) invite countries not members of the Special Union which are members of WIPO or party to the Paris Convention, intergovernmental organizations specialized in marks, and representative NGOs to be represented by observers or to participate in discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates broad technical input; at least one member of invited intergovernmental organizations must be a party to the Agreement (Article 5(2)(a)–(c), Article 5(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of the Committee of Experts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee of Experts shall: (i) make amendments and additions to the Classification; (ii) address recommendations to facilitate use and promote uniform application; (iii) take measures (without financial implications) to help developing countries apply the Classification; (iv) may establish subcommittees and working groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee's mandate includes technical development, harmonization, capacity support for developing countries, and delegation to subgroups (Article 5(3)(i)–(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal submission and communication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for amendments or additions may be made by competent Offices, the International Bureau, represented intergovernmental organizations, and specially invited countries/organizations; proposals shall be communicated to the International Bureau, which shall submit them to Committee members and observers not later than two months before the session at which they are to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures advance circulation of amendment proposals to permit consideration (Article 5(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making and voting thresholds in the Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of the Committee of Experts require a simple majority of the countries represented and voting; decisions regarded by one-fifth as modifying the basic structure or entailing substantial reclassification require a three-fourths majority; abstentions are not votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines ordinary vs significant-change voting rules and voting counting method (Article 5(6)(b)–(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and entry into force of Committee amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Every decision of the Committee concerning adoption of amendments/additions and recommendations shall be notified by the International Bureau to the competent Offices; amendments and additions shall enter into force six months after the date of dispatch of the notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Bureau handles notification; six-month delay before amendments take effect (Article 6(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation and publication of amendments by the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall incorporate in the Classification the amendments and additions which have entered into force and shall publish announcements of them in periodicals designated by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau updates the official Classification and arranges for public announcement (Article 6(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly composition and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Union shall have an Assembly consisting of the countries of the Special Union; each government is represented by one delegate (who may be assisted), and intergovernmental organizations may be represented by observers if the Assembly decides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly is the plenary decision-making body for maintenance and development of the Special Union (Article 7(1)(a)–(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly functions and powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Article 5, the Assembly shall deal with matters concerning maintenance/development of the Special Union, give directions to the International Bureau, review/approve Director General reports, determine program and adopt biennial budget, adopt financial regulations, decide on official texts in other languages, establish committees/working groups, admit observers, and take other actions to further objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly has broad governance, budgetary and policy roles for the Special Union (Article 7(2)(a)(i)–(x)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly voting, quorum and meeting frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Assembly member has one vote; one-half of members constitute a quorum; decisions of the Assembly require two-thirds of votes cast (subject to Article 11(2)); Assembly meets once every two years in ordinary session and may meet extraordinarily upon convocation at request of one-fourth of members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of quorum permits provisional decisions that later require written confirmation; abstentions not counted as votes (Article 7(3)(a)–(4)(a)–(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau and Director General responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative tasks concerning the Special Union are performed by the International Bureau; the Director General is chief executive, prepares meetings and provides secretariat, participates without vote, transmits certified copies of Agreement/amendments/classification, registers Agreement with UN, notifies Governments of specified events, and acts as ex officio secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau and Director General manage administration, communications, and preparations for revision conferences and meetings (Article 8(1)–(4); Article 17(3)–(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget composition and financing sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Union shall have a budget including income/expenses proper to it, contributions to common budgets, and sums for the Conference budget; budget financed from contributions of countries, fees/charges for services, sale/royalties of publications, gifts/bequests/subventions, rents/interests and miscellaneous income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines permitted revenue sources and coordination with budgets of other Unions (Article 9(1)–(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of annual contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: For contribution purposes each country of the Special Union shall belong to the same class as it belongs in the Paris Union and shall pay its annual contribution on the basis of the same number of units fixed for that class; the annual contribution of each country is proportional to its units relative to total units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions due on January 1; arrears may affect voting rights (Article 9(4)(a)–(c),(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of voting rights for arrears
rubrics_metrics.description: A country in arrears in payment of contributions may not exercise its right to vote in any organ of the Special Union if its arrears equal or exceed contributions due for the preceding two full years; exception possible if organ is satisfied delay is due to exceptional/unavoidable circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial compliance condition tied to governance participation (Article 9(4)(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Working capital fund and advances
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Union shall have a working capital fund constituted by a single payment by each country; if insufficient, Assembly shall decide to increase it; in HQ agreement the host country shall grant advances when fund insufficient; terms and rights to denounce advances are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly fixes proportions and terms of payments; host country may provide advances under separate agreements (Article 9(6)–(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditing of accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditing of the accounts shall be effected by one or more of the countries of the Special Union or by external auditors, to be designated by the Assembly with their agreement, as provided in financial regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly designates auditors (Article 9(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision conferences and amendment procedures (Articles 7,8,9,11)
rubrics_metrics.description: This Agreement may be revised by a special conference; proposals to amend Articles 7, 8, 9 and Article 11 may be initiated by any country or the Director General and must be communicated six months in advance; amendments to these Articles shall be adopted by the Assembly requiring three-fourths of votes cast (and amendments to Article 7 and the present paragraph require four-fifths).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption thresholds are higher for core governance/financial provisions; advanced notice required (Article 10, Article 11(1)–(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force of certain amendments and binding effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to Articles 7,8,9,11 shall enter into force one month after written notifications of acceptance have been received by the Director General from three-fourths of the countries members at the time the amendment was adopted; such amendments bind all countries which accepted them as specified, with special treatment for amendments increasing financial obligations (bind only those who notified acceptance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes acceptance/entry into force timing and scope of binding effect, especially for financial obligations (Article 11(3)(a)–(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming party: eligibility and instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any country party to the Paris Convention may become party to this Agreement by signature followed by deposit of instrument of ratification, or by deposit of an instrument of accession; instruments shall be deposited with the Director General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (3) references Article 24 of the Stockholm Act; accession rules connect to Paris Convention membership (Article 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force of the Agreement for states
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to the first five countries which have deposited instruments of ratification or accession, the Agreement enters into force three months after the fifth instrument is deposited; for any other country it enters into force three months after the date on which its ratification or accession was notified by the Director General unless a later date is indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides specific triggering rules for initial and subsequent parties (Article 13(1)–(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of the Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement shall have the same duration as the Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ties Agreement lifetime to the Paris Convention (Article 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation (withdrawal) procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any country may denounce the Agreement by notification to the Director General; denunciation takes effect one year after receipt of notification; a country may not denounce before five years from its date of becoming a member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets waiting period before denunciation and one-year delay to take effect (Article 15(1)–(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute settlement default and opt-out
rubrics_metrics.description: Any dispute between countries concerning interpretation or application not settled by negotiation may be brought before the International Court of Justice unless the countries agree on another method; any country may declare on signature or deposit that it does not consider itself bound by the ICJ provision (opt-out).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a country makes such a declaration, paragraph (1) does not apply to disputes involving that country; declarations may be withdrawn at any time (Article 16(1)–(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, depositary and transmission duties of Director General
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement shall be signed in a single original in English and French and deposited with the Director General; the Director General shall transmit certified copies of the signed text and any amendment on request, furnish certified copies of the Classification on request, register the Agreement with the UN, and notify Governments of specified events (signatures, deposits, entry into force, declarations, withdrawals, acceptances and dates, denunciations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed list of Director General's communications and depositary functions (Article 17(1)–(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Committee and preparatory resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending entry into force of the Agreement, a provisional Committee of Experts is set up at the International Bureau including representatives of each country having signed or acceded; it shall reexamine the Classification and prepare draft amendments/additions as necessary and the Bureau shall prepare the work and convene the provisional Committee when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional Committee operates prior to entry into force and transmits drafts to the permanent Committee when Agreement enters into force (Resolution following treaty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expense responsibility for delegates/observers
rubrics_metrics.description: The expenses (travel and subsistence) of members of the provisional Committee and of observers shall be borne by the countries or organizations which they represent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegations pay their own participation costs (Resolution point 7).
